&reftitle.setup;
&reftitle.required;
Installation requirements on non-Windows platforms
ImageMagick >= 6.2.4 is required. The amount of file formats supported by Imagick depends entirely upon the amount of formats supported by your ImageMagick installation. For example, Imagemagick requires ghostscript to conduct PDF operations.
&reftitle.install;
&pecl.moved;
As of Imagick 3.8.0, the recommended way to install this extension is with &link.pie;, the PHP Installer for Extensions, using the imagick/imagick package.
Installing Imagick with PIE
pie install imagick/imagick
On non-Windows platforms, PIE builds the extension from source, so the ImageMagick development files have to be installed beforehand. If ImageMagick is installed in a non-standard location, its installation prefix can be passed with the --with-imagick configure option.
Installing Imagick with PIE against a custom ImageMagick prefix
pie install imagick/imagick --with-imagick=/opt/imagemagick
When a project declares the extension as a requirement in its composer.json, running pie install without any argument in the project directory checks the extensions required by the project and offers to install the missing ones.
Requiring Imagick in a project's composer.json
{ "require": { "ext-imagick": "*" } }
On Windows, PIE downloads a prebuilt package matching the PHP version, thread safety and architecture of the target PHP installation instead of building the extension. The extension DLL (php_imagick.dll) is installed into the extension_dir, and the bundled ImageMagick DLLs are copied next to php.exe.
The same prebuilt Windows packages can also be downloaded manually from the GitHub releases page. In that case, the extension DLL needs to be put into the extension_dir and renamed to php_imagick.dll, and the ImageMagick DLLs need to be put somewhere in the PATH.
As of Imagick 3.6.0, the prebuilt Windows packages also contain ImageMagick XML configuration files in config; when installing with PIE, these are copied to extras\imagick\config in the PHP installation directory. To use these instead of the built-in defaults, they need to be put into %USERPROFILE%/.config/ImageMagick, or alternatively in the path given by the environment variable MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH. Refer to the ImageMagick configuration files documentation for further details.
The official name of this extension is imagick.
Releases prior to Imagick 3.8.0 can be found in the Imagick PECL package.
